header.function_name: TBD Crossdock Master Setting - Part List

revisions.author: Ivan Rayhan
revisions.description: Initial draft based on the business decisions for the Crossdock Master Setting Part List sub-menu and the crossdockpoc web prototype as of 12-Oct-26. Upload backend is documented in UISS-Batch "Crossdock Master Setting - Part List Upload". Data level: TB_M_PART_CANDIDATE is at part number level (key PART_NO, no calculation period); TB_M_PART_CANDIDATE_DEST (Mapping per Destination) is at part number + calculation period + destination level.

objective: To register crossdock candidate parts (Part No, Minimum MAD, Pcs/Case, Max Case/Day, Effective Start Date).
To search and display registered crossdock parts with their status, capacity and mapping completeness.
To change part data and part status (Candidate / Active / Inactive) of a registered part.
To display the change history of a part.
To export the Part List to Excel and upload part settings from Excel (Add and Edit).
This sub-menu is opened only for users logged in with a Procurement account; users with a D/S account open the Mapping per Destination sub-menu instead.

items: The sub-menu is opened only for users logged in with a Procurement account.
Search criteria: 'Part Number' and 'Part Name' blank, 'Status' = All, 'Sort by' = Newer to Older.
Retrieve all parts of TB_M_PART_CANDIDATE and display them sorted by CHANGED_DT descending, 25 rows per page, page 1.
If no part is registered at all, hide the table and display message no. 2 with [Upload Excel] and [Add one part].
'Part Number' and 'Part Name' match by 'contains', case-insensitive; 'Status' matches exactly. All criteria are combined with AND.
Changing any criterion, 'Sort by' or 'Rows per page' returns the list to page 1.
The prototype applies the filter while typing. TBD: whether filtering waits for [Search] or the [Search] button is removed.
If no row matches, hide the table and paging and display message no. 1 with [Reset filter].
Counter 'N parts · M incomplete mappings' is counted over the whole filtered result, not only the current page.

Incomplete mapping: the part has no destination in TB_M_PART_CANDIDATE_DEST, or the sum of destination CASE_DAY differs from MAX_CASE_DAY. Mark the row with a blue bar and count it in 'M incomplete mappings'.
Min MAD flag: show 'Min MAD' bold in warning colour when the 6-month average MAD is below MIN_MAD, except for status Candidate (no MAD history yet). Source of the MAD history is TBD.
Total Pcs/Day = Pcs/Case x Max Case/Day.
Open the 'Add Part Candidate Crossdock' modal. 'Status' = Candidate and locked (a new part is always Candidate); 'Effective Start Date' = system date + 1 day, minimum today.
'Part No' lists parts of TB_M_PART_MASTER that are not yet registered in TB_M_PART_CANDIDATE, so a Part No cannot be duplicated. No match shows message no. 8.
Selecting a Part No autofills 'Part Name'. 'Max Case/Day' is locked until 'Pcs/Case' is filled.

[Save] is enabled only when Part No, Pcs/Case > 0 and Max Case/Day > 0 are filled; otherwise its tooltip shows message no. 5, 6 or 7 for the first missing item. Effective Start Date and Minimum MAD are not mandatory (TBD: confirm).
If the Part No was registered by another user in the meantime, display message no. 3. Stop.
Insert the part into TB_M_PART_CANDIDATE with PART_STATUS = Candidate and SYNC_STATUS = 0 (No Sync) (refer Data Edit Mapping).
Insert the change history (TBD: history table and logged events not defined yet).
Close the modal, reset the Part Number / Part Name / Status filters, sort Newer to Older and display message no. 9. The new part is shown at the top.

operation.text: User clicks [Cancel] or the X icon: close the modal without saving.
User clicks the 'Part Number' link or [Edit] on a row.

items: Open the 'Edit part data' modal with the saved values. 'Part No' is locked; 'Status' can be Candidate / Active / Inactive.
'Effective Start Date' is editable only while the saved status is Candidate (minimum today); otherwise locked with message no. 10 as tooltip.
'Minimum MAD', 'Pcs/Case' and 'Max Case/Day' can be changed; 'Total Pcs/Day' is recalculated.
If the record was changed by another user after it was opened, display message no. 4. Stop.
Update TB_M_PART_CANDIDATE and set SYNC_STATUS = 0 (No Sync), CHANGED_BY and CHANGED_DT. Every Save returns the part to No Sync so the D/S user synchronises it again.
Insert the change history (TBD: history table and logged events not defined yet).
Close the modal, move the part to the top of the list and display message no. 9.
User clicks the clock icon on a row: open 'History setting' with the change timeline of the part, newest first.
Each event shows the title, date-time, field name, old value (struck through) → new value and user.
A part without history shows message no. 12. TBD: history source, logged events and retention.
User clicks [Upload Excel]: open the modal with the template columns, the rules and the file area (.xlsx, max 5 MB, max 5,000 rows).
Edit rows use sheet 'Upload' of the Part List Export Excel as base file (pre-filled with flag E).
Status rule: a Candidate part's status cannot be changed by upload; Active <-> Inactive can be changed; no part can be changed to Candidate.

User clicks [Validate file] (save button of the upload): the file is passed to the upload batch; validation, saving (all-or-nothing) and logging follow UISS-Batch "Crossdock Master Setting - Part List Upload".
When the upload is completed, close the modal and display message no. 11. When it is rejected, show the batch result (error list) - refer UISS-Batch.
Changed parts show Sync Status No Sync.
User clicks [Export Excel]: download Crossdock_Part_List_YYYYMMDD.xlsx.

Sheet 'Part List': rows of the active filter and sort (all pages) with Part Number, Part Name, Min MAD, Pcs/Case, Max Case/Day, Total Pcs/Day, Status, Effective Start Date, Last Update. Information only.
Sheet 'Upload': every registered part with part_no, minimum_mad, pcs_case, max_case_day, status, flag_add_edit = E, effective_start_date (DD-Mon-YYYY). Base file for Edit uploads.
If the file cannot be created, display message no. 13.
